stage_1.assessment:
All SPEC COMPLIANCE deliverables verified:
1. event:folder frames with JSON entry data — implementation writes `event: folder\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(entry)}\n\n` per onProgress call; test confirms presence.
2. Terminal event:done with full {entries, scannedAt, partial} — scanAll returns exactly this shape; done frame emitted.
3. Disconnect aborts stream without error — res.on('close') triggers AbortController.abort(); raceDeadline races abort signal; route guards done write with !abortController.signal.aborted; test confirms no done after destroy, zero uncaught errors, server remains healthy.
4. GET /api/scan fallback unchanged — route order places /api/scan/stream before /api/scan; /api/scan handler unmodified; existing scan tests all pass.
5. Security headers/CSP preserved on SSE — writeHead spreads securityHeaders() alongside content-type text/event-stream; CSP test suite passes.
6. No new dependencies, no WebSockets — only vanilla Node http/fs/promises used; package.json unchanged.
7. access_denied/partial entries keep status and reason — makeEntry includes reason for these statuses; entries streamed as-is.
8. Frame shape stable for T7 — event:folder / event:done with documented JSON payloads; T7 execution plan references parsing these frames.

strengths: Clean abort plumbing: AbortController wired through context.abortSignal → raceDeadline → walkFolder timeout path, with listener cleanup in finally blocks
Real-filesystem fixture test validates full contract (headers, folder frames, done payload shape)
Abort test uses hanging fs stub to verify cleanup without relying on timing; asserts readdirCount==1, no done, no uncaught errors, server health
Frame format matches EventSource standard and T7 client expectations
stage_2.assessment: Implementation meets all quality bar criteria. Tests written before implementation (per pocket workflow), both stream contract and abort cleanup tests present. All 32 existing tests pass. No regressions to /api/scan. No external dependencies introduced. Zero listener leaks (onClose removed in finally). The abort path uses res.on('close') instead of req.on('close') — functionally equivalent for detecting client disconnect and marginally more robust.
